added_failures_note: measured by the reviewer: base arm 1838c759 tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py 13 passed EXIT=0 (arming/base.log); head arm e3ac8d01 tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py 16 passed EXIT=0 (arming/head.log); neither arm reports a FAILED or ERROR id, so 0 failures are added. The reviewed run is an implement node and declares no baseline_suite or after_suite (both absent from its manifest and null in its classification), so the count comes from base and head arms the reviewer ran in scratch trees under TMPDIR, not from the reviewed run's own suite logs.
call_sites: one production call site: run_signals_stage (imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py) is the signals stage entry the CLI drives, and it is the only caller that builds the reset extra_filter; build_focus_predicate is a shared helper already consumed by the signals claim path, so no second reset path was minted.

findings.text: follow-on for the coordinator: the live read-only receipt shows the focused reset filter admits exactly the named source's 14 members (focus_filter_selected=14 == member_count=14) but the status-gated reset count for that source is 0, because all 14 members are already status 'discovered' while the reset-to-discovered spec gates on status IN [enriched, underspecified, checked]. So the receipt proves the filter narrows scope but does not exercise an actual focused reset end-to-end; a source with enriched members is needed to show the reset path fires on the focused cohort and not the 4679-signal whole-facility cohort. The run's manifest evidence_inputs states this honestly.

follow-on: the gate's fake GraphClient (_Catalogue) re-implements the focus resolution in Python -- id/accessor identity, direct source_id, and data_source_path segment membership -- rather than driving the real Cypher, so the reset query's MEMBER_OF/source-array traversal is covered only structurally (the test asserts the substring 'n.id IN $focus_items' is present) and the actual graph predicate is not executed by any test. The branch behaviour (filter present with focus, absent without) is asserted; the predicate's graph semantics are taken on trust from build_focus_predicate's existing coverage.

item_verdicts.call_sites: one production call site: run_signals_stage (imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py) is the signals stage entry the CLI drives, and it is the only caller that builds the reset extra_filter; build_focus_predicate is a shared helper already consumed by the signals claim path, so no second reset path was minted.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 1838c759. e3ac8d01 changes imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py in the --reset-to branch: it imports build_focus_predicate alongside build_category_predicate, appends the focus predicate to extra_filter and adds the focus_items query parameter when focus is set, and adds `focus: <items>` to the reset log scope string; the comment now reads 'scanner, category and focus scope'. It adds tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py (206 lines, 3 tests) with a fake GraphClient catalogue that resolves focus to sources` but falls back to member-source membership on unfocus` and an unas` status guard is run to prove the unnamed-source signal keeps its status. It adds the evidence fragment (45 lines).
item_verdicts.done_when: the measure has three parts: tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py shows a focused reset passes a build_focus_predicate filter and the focus items into reset_to_status while an unnamed source's signal keeps its status; tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py still passes; and a read-only live count of FacilitySignals the focused reset filter selects for --focus with the MDAC magPbTCNNN SignalSource id equals that source's member count. Parts one and two are met: the reviewer's head arm runs both files at e3ac8d01 to 16 passed, EXIT=0, and the base arm runs test_signals_focus.py at 1838c759 to 13 passed, EXIT=0. Part three is met by the reviewed run's own read-only live_count.log: member_count=14, focus_filter_selected=14, focus_equals_members=True (whole_facility_eligible=4679). The same log records reset_status_gated_selected=0, which the review treats as an honest caveat on the receipt rather than a shortfall of the filter.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to make the signals --reset-to branch apply the --focus filter so a focused reset touches only the focused sources. The diff in run_signals_stage (imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py) adds `if focus_items: extra_filter += f" {build_focus_predicate('n', focus_items)}"` and `extra_params["focus_items"] = focus_items` to the reset branch, and extends the reset log scope with `focus: ...`. That is exactly the mechanism the goal names, and it reuses the same predicate the section 1 enrichment/check claims use.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the reviewed manifest records status complete, commit e3ac8d011fe4f996435f771081243d71771fed42, the gate `tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py -> 16 passed, EXIT=0`, a negative_control_log path, and artifacts/evidence_inputs describing the live count. The reviewed run is an implement node, so baseline_suite and after_suite are absent from its manifest and null in its classification; the added-failure figure below was therefore measured from base and head arms the reviewer ran at 1838c759 and e3ac8d01.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --name-status 1838c759..e3ac8d01 lists exactly docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/focused-reset-scope.html (A), imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py (M) and tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py (A), three paths all inside the declared four-path fence (the fourth, docs/figures/.../focused-reset-scope, was not needed since the done-when names no figure), with no generated model and nothing outside it.

justifications.durability: the guard is real and mutation-sensitive: dropping the focus block reddens the unnamed-source test (2 failed, EXIT=1) and the unmutated head passes 16 at the gate. Coverage gaps, both follow-ons not blockers: the new test drives a fake GraphClient that re-implements the focus resolution in Python, so the real predicate's MEMBER_OF/source-array traversal is asserted only structurally (substring presence of n.id IN $focus_items) and never executed against a live graph; and the live receipt shows reset_status_gated_selected=0 for the named source, so no executed reset proves the end-to-end 'focused reset touches only the focused sources' claim -- the filter is proven, the reset count is not.
justifications.evidence: I ran both arms in scratch trees under TMPDIR: base 1838c759 tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py collected 13, 0 failed, EXIT=0; head e3ac8d01 tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py tests/discovery/test_signals_focus.py collected 16, 0 failed, EXIT=0, so the diff adds no failure. I independently reproduced the reviewed run's declared mutation (drop the focus filter block from the reset branch) against my head tree: tests/discovery/test_signals_focus_reset.py then reports 2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1 with test_unnamed_source_signal_keeps_its_status among the failures, matching the run's own negative_control.log, while the unmutated head passes 3/3. The live count is the run's own read-only receipt (focus_filter_selected 14 == member_count 14), which I did not re-verified live because the reviewed run's receipt is the evidence the measure cites and I hold no independent graph execution in the time budget.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's existing shape: it appends an AND-prefixed predicate string to extra_filter and a matching extra_params key, exactly as the scanner and category filters already do, and it reuses the canonical build_focus_predicate rather than spelling a second focus predicate inline. The reset log scope string follows the existing scope_parts idiom.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is present in the reset branch: focus_items now feeds build_focus_predicate into the reset extra_filter and is passed as a query parameter, exactly the mechanism the goal names, and the reset log scope names the focus so an operator sees the narrowing. The change is the minimal form of the goal and mirrors the scanner/category scoping that was already there.
justifications.reuse: the diff reuses build_focus_predicate -- the same helper the section 1 claims use -- so the reset and the claims narrow by one shared predicate, and it does not duplicate the focus resolution helper or invent a reset-specific filter. No duplicated constant or parallel mechanism was introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status 1838c759..e3ac8d01 lists exactly three paths, all inside the declared fence, with no generated model and nothing outside it; the reviewed manifest's changed_paths match the three landed paths.
